text:
alex: Bringing up lyra-22b (int8) on canary, seeing two issues: quality delta on long-form prompts and occasional OOMs at p99 when batch sizes spike. Logs attached below.
lina: can you paste the exact config you used for canary? batch_size, max_new_tokens, prefetch?
alex: config: batch_size=16, max_new_tokens=512, prefetch=enabled, kv_cache_prefetch=auto. Serving on g5x2 nodes. note: memory fragmentation jumps after ~3k requests.
ben: 16 is pretty aggressive for a 22B model with int8 kv overhead. try lowering default batch to 8 and add a per-request cap on tokens.
alex: ok will try batch=8. but quality regression worry: discrete drop when switching to int8 on a subset of prompts (mostly code-generation). perplexity delta ~+6%.
nora: for quantization quality, do you use per-channel or symmetric quant? we saw code-gen regressions with naive asymmetric quant. also check activation clipping.
alex: used static symmetric per-tensor quant (our generic pipeline). activation clip was default 8.0.
lina: try per-channel for attentions and MLP if pipeline supports it. also run a small eval set with prompt-preserve and top-p sampling to compare.
ben: about OOMs: is KV cache eviction enabled? we had cases where prefetch created transient large allocations then slab fragmentation prevented reuse.
alex: KV eviction was off for canary. prefetch writes almost-full KV pages then some requests allocate extra 1-2GB.
nora: Enable kv_eviction=tail_trim and set prefetch_budget=0.6 (60% of kv pool). Also enable small-allocation-compact every 5m.
alex: quick experiment results: batch=8 removed p95 latency spike, p99 OOM still rare but reproduced once in 2k requests.
ci-bot: Deploy canary-lyra22b-int8-v2 started at 1719004410 by alex
lina: if OOM persists, add a hard cap on max_new_tokens per-request for canary (e.g., 384) so adversarial requests don't blow up memory.
ben: also tweak allocator tune: MADV_DONTNEED after KV trim to return pages to OS; set jemalloc background_thread to true. we had fragmentation drop by ~30%.
nora: small code snippet that helped before:

```
# server config
model.lyra22b.kv_cache_prefetch = false
model.lyra22b.kv_eviction = "tail_trim"
model.lyra22b.prefetch_budget = 0.6
runtime.jemalloc.background_thread = true
runtime.madvise.on_trim = "MADV_DONTNEED"
```

alex: ran that locally, fragmentation metric improved. re-ran eval for regressions: int8 per-channel reduced code-gen delta to +1.2% (still small but much better).
lina: run 1000-shot canary with synthetic long-code prompts to ensure no silent regressions near max_new_tokens boundary.
ben: also propose adaptive-batching: if request.tokens_total > 1024 then route to small-batch queue (batch cap 4). reduces memory pressure.
alex: implemented adaptive route rule & enforced max_new_tokens=384 for canary. testing now.
nora: create a quick alert for kv-frag growth: if kv_frag_ratio > 0.25 for 10m -> create ticket and rollback trigger. we hit this previously and it helped.
alex: results after changes: no OOM in 10k requests, p99 latency within SLO, quality diff down to +0.9% on eval set. will push to canary rollout tomorrow.
lina: nice. open a short PR describing changes (batch default 8, max_new_tokens 384, kv_eviction tail_trim, jemalloc tune) and add the eval artifacts.
alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4281
ben: add a note in model-onboarding checklist: always run per-channel quant ablation for codegen-heavy models before promoting int8 as default.
nora: and add a canary-runbook snippet for kv fragmentation detection + remedial commands.
alex: tagging followups: @lina to add eval artifacts, @ben to draft allocator doc, @nora to update runbook. thanks everyone :tada!
